gap: No result ChatGPT got works out how bright the picture will be. The rule (from Elite Screens' own article) is foot-lamberts = projector ANSI lumens ÷ screen area in sq ft × gain, with SMPTE 196M's minimum of 12 fL and ideal of 16 fL in a dark room. By that math, a 200-ANSI-lumen portable projector like the Aurzen EAZZE D1G gives only about 5 fL on a 120-inch, 1.1-gain portable screen. That projector reaches 16 fL only at about 68 inches, and a 120-inch, 1.1-gain screen needs about 620 lumens to get there.
standout_why: I opened projectorverdict.com best-projector-screen and best-tripod-projector-screen, itechguides.com outdoor screens, projectorreviews.com buyer's guide and austingallery.org best-projector-screens-2026. None of them gives a lumens, foot-lambert or nits formula, a target brightness or a lumens-to-size number. austingallery comes closest, saying only that 'the same projector light spread across double the area is half as bright per inch' and 'a dim projector becomes unwatchable at this area', with no numbers. projectorverdict and itechguides cover only the Yard Master 2 wind limit (7 mph) and that it is front-projection only. I could not open the cited Wirecutter page (403 through the proxy, blocked on nytimes.com) or esquire.com (blocked), so they were not checked.
decides: The finding sets the screen size and favours higher gain rather than naming one product. ChatGPT's default advice of 100–120 inches only works with a projector of about 400–620 ANSI lumens. A shopper with a 200–300-lumen portable projector should buy about 70–80 inches, or accept a dim picture. At the same size and lumens, the Yard Master 2's 1.3 gain gives 18% more brightness than the 1.1-gain Elite Tripod and Aurzen screens (1.3 ÷ 1.1). So it is the better pick of ChatGPT's choices when the projector is dim, as long as it is sized down.

findings.label: Brightness formula (maker's own words)
findings.value: Divide the projector's lumens by the screen area in ft² to get foot-lamberts, then multiply by the screen gain to get image luminance. Elite's example: 1,000 lumens on a 100-inch 16:9 screen (about 30 ft²) gives about 33 fL at 1.0 gain and about 50 at 1.5 gain.
findings.source_title: ANSI Lumens, Foot Lamberts, & Image Luminance – Elite Screens Tech Tip
findings.note: The page shows no publication date; the 2016/04 date is inferred from the URL. AWOL Valerion's blog (https://www.valerion.com/blog/understanding-projector-brightness-lumens-ansi-lumens-iso-lumens-lux-foot-lamberts-and-nits, dated 2025-04-15, read 2026-11-08) gives the same equation in one line: 'Foot-Lamberts = (lumens of projector × gain of screen) ÷ area of screen (in square feet)'. It also gives nits = fL × 3.426.

findings.label: Target screen brightness, dark room (SMPTE 196M as cited by Elite Screens)
findings.value: 16 fL ideal, 12 fL minimum, 22 fL maximum. About 50 fL is recommended with ambient light.
findings.source_title: ANSI Lumens, Foot Lamberts, & Image Luminance – Elite Screens Tech Tip
findings.note: Elite also gives 14 fL for film playback. Valerion gives 14–16 fL for cinema and 12–30 fL as good for home theaters.

findings.value: CineWhite UHD-B, 1.3 gain, 180° viewing angle, black-backed ('eliminates light penetration'), front projection only
findings.source_title: Yard Master 2 | Best Outdoor Movie Projector Screen - Elite Screen
findings.note: Sizes are 58, 75, 90, 105, 120, 125 and 140 inches (16:9). Elite gives two different wind limits: 'up to 7 mph' in the description and 'below 10mph' in the FAQ.

findings.label: Projector brightness
findings.source_title: Aurzen EAZZE D1G Google TV Smart Projector
findings.note: From storecheck.py search of aurzen.com; the listing reads 'Authentic 200 ANSI Lumens brightness'. The same search showed the EAZZE D1R at 280 ANSI lumens and the D1R air at 300 ANSI lumens.

findings.label: Estimated brightness with a 200-ANSI-lumen portable projector
findings.source_title: ANSI Lumens, Foot Lamberts, & Image Luminance – Elite Screens Tech Tip
findings.note: Area of a 16:9 screen = 0.4273 × D² in², so 120 inches = 6,153 in² = 42.73 ft². Brightness = 200 ÷ 42.73 × 1.1 = 5.15 fL, which is below SMPTE's 12 fL minimum. A 300-lumen projector (D1R air) gives 7.7 fL. Reaching 16 fL on this screen needs 16 × 42.73 ÷ 1.1 = 622 lumens. This is a calculated estimate; it ignores lamp/LED dimming in eco or colour-accurate modes.

findings.label: Estimated brightness with a 200-ANSI-lumen projector, 105-inch size
findings.value: About 7.9 fL. Reaching 16 fL needs about 403 lumens.
findings.source_title: Yard Master 2 | Best Outdoor Movie Projector Screen - Elite Screen
findings.note: 105 inches = 0.4273 × 11,025 = 4,711 in² = 32.72 ft². 200 ÷ 32.72 × 1.3 = 7.95 fL. Lumens for 16 fL = 16 × 32.72 ÷ 1.3 = 403. Uses Elite's formula with the 1.3 gain from the product page.

findings.label: Largest 16:9 screen a 200-ANSI-lumen projector can light to SMPTE targets
findings.value: About 68 inches (16 fL) or about 79 inches (12 fL) at 1.1 gain; about 74 inches (16 fL) at 1.3 gain
findings.source_title: ANSI Lumens, Foot Lamberts, & Image Luminance – Elite Screens Tech Tip
findings.note: Area = lumens × gain ÷ fL, then D = √(area × 144 ÷ 0.4273). At 1.1 gain and 16 fL: 200 × 1.1 ÷ 16 = 13.75 ft², giving D = 68.1 in. At 12 fL: 18.33 ft², giving D = 78.6 in. At 1.3 gain and 16 fL: 16.25 ft², giving D = 74.1 in.
